Salle 3, deuxième étage. On n'y interrog:
Room 3, second floor. Nobody has been questioned here since the Section moved its interviews to the basement. The power is off; the key was in the door.

Three places, perhaps four, before the caretaker comes back up. This is where people were brought in March 1971, on the evenings the clock ran slow.
Elle retarde de douze minutes sur votre: It runs twelve minutes slow against your watch. Under the dial, a plate: "Set by order of the Cabinet. Do not touch." Under the plate, scratched into the brass: "A. V. 9.3.71". Your father opened this clock.
Le registre des passages, dans le classe: The visitors' register, in the filing cabinet
Mars 1971. Les soirs du 2, du 9 et du 16: March 1971. On the evenings of the 2nd, 9th and 16th, the exit times written here don't match the corridor's: twelve minutes apart, every time. Twelve minutes during which, on paper, nobody was in the room. The exits are all signed in the same hand.
La table vissée au sol: The table bolted to the floor
Des initiales, des dates, gravées au can: Initials, dates, carved with a penknife by hands that were waiting. Among them, in small careful capitals: "16.3: THE CLOCK LIES".
Derrière la vitre, la salle d'observatio: Behind the glass, the observation room, empty. A chair turned towards you, a camera tripod without a camera. From there, they watched. You wonder which side of the glass your father sat on.
Vous refermez la salle 3. Dans le couloi: You lock Room 3 again. In the corridor, the Section clock shows the same time as your watch. The one in the room, behind the door, goes on running slow for nobody.
